description.value: The study examined salience-network activity and directed functional interactions between the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral anterior insulae during four perceptual decision-making tasks with varying difficulty.

design.value: Participants completed four perceptual decision-making tasks involving visual and audiovisual stimuli while behavioral performance and fMRI-BOLD data were collected. Task difficulty was manipulated through stimulus noise, audiovisual asynchrony, or random-dot-motion coherence, and task-dependent activity and directed functional connectivity were examined.

name.value: F.A.C.E. Training-an interactive training by Paul Ekman

source_definition.value: Noise level or ambiguity in the sensory information was used to vary task difficulty.
Images were degraded with 0%, 40%, and 55% noise in the face-house task and 0% and 40% noise in the happy-angry face task.
The six motion parameters were entered as nuisance covariates and were regressed out of the data.

description.value: There were 32 human participants (16 males, 16 females; mean age±standard deviation=27.6±4.7 years) who completed all four experimental tasks. One more male participant took part in face-house discrimination and in audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception tasks.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal or corrected to normal vision

exclusion_criteria.value: No red/green color blindness was reported.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated face and house images degraded with 0%, 40%, and 55% noise.

instructions.value: Indicate whether the presented picture was a house or face as quickly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 14 images of faces and 14 images of houses, equalized for luminance and degraded by image pixel phase randomization with Gaussian noise.

task_description.value: Participants discriminated happy and angry faces presented as clear or noisy images.

instructions.value: Indicate whether the face was happy or angry.

stimuli.value: Two sets of human face images, a happy set and an angry set, with 0% or 40% noise.

task_name.value: audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception task

task_description.value: Participants judged whether auditory and visual stimuli were synchronous or asynchronous across varying stimulus onset asynchronies.

instructions.value: Report synchrony or asynchrony by button press.

stimuli.value: A 440-Hz, 30-ms tone paired with a 30-ms yellow-red disc flash.

task_name.value: random dot motion direction discrimination task

task_description.value: Participants discriminated leftward versus rightward motion in noisy random-dot displays with varying coherence and color coherence.

instructions.value: Report whether the dots moved leftward or rightward.

stimuli.value: Randomly moving red and green dots within a circular aperture, with 12%, 20%, and 100% coherence conditions.

instrument.value: 3-Tesla Siemens scanner available at the Georgia State University and Georgia Institute of Technology Center for Advanced Brain Imaging

description.value: T2*-weighted gradient echo-planar imaging protocol; field of view=204×204mm, matrix size=68×68, 37 axial slices each of 3mm thickness.
High-resolution anatomical images were acquired for anatomical references using a magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo sequence.

MRI data were analyzed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8), including slice timing correction, motion correction, coregistration to the individual anatomical image, normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and spatial smoothing.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8; Wellcome Trust Center, London)

steps.value: normalization to Montreal Neurological Institute template
spatial smoothing with an 8-mm isotropic Gaussian kernel
hemodynamic deconvolution for each ROI data

model_settings.value: At the first level, a separate GLM was specified according to task sequences and behavioral responses for each participant. Correct trials for each condition, rest, and six motion parameters were included.

estimator.value: random-effect, model-based, univariate statistical analysis; second-level one-sample t-test

model_settings.value: Deconvolved fMRI-BOLD time series were modeled using autoregressive processes; the optimal model order was selected by comparing nonparametric and parametric power spectra. Time-domain causality values were obtained by integrating causality spectra over the entire frequency range. Conditional Granger causality was used to rule out mediated interactions.

estimator.value: random permutation surrogate thresholding with at least 1000 permutations; paired t-tests on time-domain Granger causality values
